answer: Agent economies monitoring a tidal inlet or falcon habitat can curb Sybil attacks via epoch-bound verifiable delay functions. Each round, an agent hashes the beacon with its key and computes sequential modular squarings to submit a succinct proof before timeout. Because the steps cannot be parallelized or shared across keys, each active identity ties up one execution thread and its energy cost. Still, attackers with custom ASICs or faster clocks can finish several chains serially per round.
